title: Elder Sambhūta: One who, when he should go slowly, goes quickly, One who, when he should go quickly, goes slowly — That fool, lacking right…
content:
Elder Sambhūta:

One who, when he should go slowly, goes quickly,
One who, when he should go quickly, goes slowly —
That fool, lacking right method, goes to suffering.

His benefit diminishes like the moon in the dark fortnight.
He meets disgrace and opposes his friends.

One who, when he should go slowly, goes slowly,
One who, when he should go quickly, goes quickly —
That wise one, with right method, goes to happiness.

His benefit is fulfilled like the moon in the bright fortnight.
He gains fame and honor, not opposing his friends.

title: Here, bhikkhus, a person himself possesses faith and also encourages others to have faith; himself possesses moral shame and encourages others to have moral shame;…
content: Here, bhikkhus, a person himself possesses faith and also encourages others to have faith; himself possesses moral shame and encourages others to have moral shame; himself possesses moral dread and encourages others to have moral dread; himself is learned and encourages others to be learned; himself is energetic and encourages others to be energetic; himself is mindful and encourages others to be mindful; himself possesses wisdom and encourages others to possess wisdom. Such a person, bhikkhus, is called a genuine person even more than a genuine person.

title: Or when there is sloth and torpor internally, he understands: 'There is sloth and torpor in me'; or when there is no sloth and torpor…
content: Or when there is sloth and torpor internally, he understands: 'There is sloth and torpor in me'; or when there is no sloth and torpor internally, he understands: 'There is no sloth and torpor in me.' And he understands how unarisen sloth and torpor arises; and he understands how arisen sloth and torpor is abandoned; and he understands how abandoned sloth and torpor will not arise in the future.

title: Elder Nun Upacālā: Mindful, with the Dhamma-eye, A bhikkhunī training the faculties, Penetrates the peaceful path, Practiced by the supreme person. Why do you not…
content:
Elder Nun Upacālā:

Mindful, with the Dhamma-eye,
A bhikkhunī training the faculties,
Penetrates the peaceful path,
Practiced by the supreme person.

Why do you not like birth?
One born enjoys sensual pleasures.
Enjoy sensual pleasures,
Do not regret it later.

One who is born is subject to death,
Hands and feet are cut off,
Killed, bound, afflicted.
Afterwards, suffering comes.

Born in the Sakya clan,
The Buddha, the undefeated one,
Taught me the Dhamma,
To overcome birth.

He taught the Noble Eightfold Path,
About suffering, the origin of suffering,
About overcoming suffering,
And the path to the end of suffering.

Having heard his words,
I live delighting in the teaching.
I have attained the three knowledges,
Done is the Buddha's teaching.

Everywhere, joy is destroyed,
The mass of delusion is shattered.
Know thus, Evil One!
You are defeated, O Death.

title: Then the Venerable Sāriputta went to the Blessed One, paid homage, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said:…
content: Then the Venerable Sāriputta went to the Blessed One, paid homage, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said: 'Venerable Sir, this entire holy life is good friendship, good companionship, good association.' - 'Good, good, Sāriputta! This entire holy life is good friendship, good companionship, good association. Sāriputta, for a bhikkhu with good friends, good companions, good associates, it can be expected that the Noble Eightfold Path will be developed, that the Noble Eightfold Path will be cultivated.'

title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, with sensual desire as cause, with sensual desire as condition, with sensual desire as reason, with sensual desire itself as cause, they engage…
content: Furthermore, bhikkhus, with sensual desire as cause, with sensual desire as condition, with sensual desire as reason, with sensual desire itself as cause, they engage in misconduct of body, misconduct of speech, misconduct of mind. Having engaged in misconduct of body, speech, and mind, after death, with the breakup of the body, they are reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Bhikkhus, such is the danger of sensual desires, bringing suffering in the future, a mass of suffering, with sensual desire as cause, with sensual desire as condition, with sensual desire as source, with sensual desire as reason.

title: - Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, and scolds the noble ones and his fellow celibates, it is impossible, it cannot happen that he will…
content: - Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, and scolds the noble ones and his fellow celibates, it is impossible, it cannot happen that he will not encounter one of these ten misfortunes. What ten? He does not attain what has not been attained; what has been attained declines; he does not become well-versed in the good Dhamma; he becomes over-conceited regarding the good Dhamma; he does not live the holy life with joy; he commits a corrupt offense; he experiences a severe illness; he becomes mentally deranged; he becomes confused at the time of death; or after death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, and scolds the noble ones and his fellow celibates, it is impossible, it cannot happen that he will not encounter one of these ten misfortunes.

title: Friends, if others should treat a bhikkhu who is not perfect, not good, not pleasant, by touching him with hands, with stones, with sticks, or…
content: Friends, if others should treat a bhikkhu who is not perfect, not good, not pleasant, by touching him with hands, with stones, with sticks, or with swords, he understands thus: 'Such is the nature of this body that hands can touch it, stones can touch it, sticks can touch it, swords can touch it. The Blessed One has said in the simile of the saw: "Bhikkhus, even if low-down bandits were to saw your limbs one by one with a two-handled saw, yet if anyone among you defiled his mind, that person would not be following my teaching." I will be energetic and diligent, not lazy. Mindfulness is established without confusion, my body is tranquil, not agitated, my mind is concentrated and unified. Now let hands touch this body, let stones touch this body, let sticks touch this body, let swords touch this body — the teaching of the Buddhas must be practiced.'

title: Householder, that noble disciple, having known that sensual desire is a defilement of the mind, abandons sensual desire, the defilement of the mind; having known…
content: Householder, that noble disciple, having known that sensual desire is a defilement of the mind, abandons sensual desire, the defilement of the mind; having known that hatred is a defilement of the mind, abandons hatred, the defilement of the mind; having known that dullness and drowsiness are defilements of the mind, abandons dullness and drowsiness, the defilements of the mind; having known that restlessness and remorse are defilements of the mind, abandons restlessness and remorse, the defilements of the mind; having known that doubt is a defilement of the mind, abandons doubt, the defilement of the mind. This, householder, is called a noble disciple of great wisdom, of wide wisdom, one who has entered the domain of clear vision, possessed of wisdom. This is called being complete in wisdom.

title: Craving, bhikkhus, is a net that makes the wandering in saṃsāra spread out, sticky; it is because of that craving that this world is destroyed,…
content: Craving, bhikkhus, is a net that makes the wandering in saṃsāra spread out, sticky; it is because of that craving that this world is destroyed, bound, tangled like a ball of thread, like a matted cocoon, like twisted muñja grass and babhaja reeds, unable to escape from the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower realm, birth and death.
